records.title: What Do Users Ask in Open-Source AI Repositories? An Empirical Study of GitHub Issues

study_extract.design: Empirical mixed categorization and issue-management analysis described in the IEEE MSR conference abstract.
study_extract.population: 576 PapersWithCode-selected AI GitHub repositories and 24,953 issue records, according to publisher abstract.
study_extract.outcome: Publisher reports runtime errors and unclear instructions among frequent issue types; this is a sampled developer-support construct, not user-task success.
study_extract.limitations: Selection from PapersWithCode, categorization reproducibility and external validity require methods/full-text appraisal.

records.title: How Do Software Developers Use GitHub Actions to Automate Their Workflows?

study_extract.design: Publisher-described observational study of GitHub Actions adoption and project activity trends.
study_extract.population: GitHub repositories studied for workflows; exact eligible N was not available from the abstract inspected.
study_extract.outcome: Publisher reports changes in rejected PR and commits on merged PRs; no randomized AI-agent productivity effect.
study_extract.limitations: Confounding by adoption timing, project lifecycle, activity-based outcomes and incomplete denominator.

records.title: Analyzing the Growth Patterns of GitHub Projects to Construct Best Practices for Project Managements
records.reason: 10-repository case study with normative star-growth interpretations; not sufficiently matched to our independent verified reuse or agent task-endpoint constructs; retain as screened exclusion.

records.title: Beyond Dependencies: The Role of Copy-Based Reuse in Open Source Software Development

study_extract.design: ACM TOSEM observational World of Code blob-origin and copy-based reuse tracing with developer survey.
study_extract.population: Publisher describes broad World of Code historical project/blob frame and 374 complete survey responses.
study_extract.outcome: Publisher reports many reused artifacts originate in small and medium projects; copy does not imply validated license compatibility or avoided labor/carbon.
study_extract.limitations: Exact byte-for-byte blob matches omit modified copies, origin can be misattributed and survey response/selection biases remain.

records.title: The Promises and Perils of Mining GitHub

study_extract.design: Methodological survey and empirical warning on GitHub mining selection and project metadata.
study_extract.population: GitHub repository mining research; no trial cohort or reuse-correctness denominator assessed in this abstract-level screen.
study_extract.outcome: Documents that repository metadata and selection mechanisms can mislead observational inference.
study_extract.limitations: Historical practices and API behavior evolved; use as validity guidance rather than estimate of current outcome.

records.title: Agentic Much? Adoption of Coding Agents on GitHub
records.reason: 2026-01-26 v1 precursor of v2 and 2026 ACM journal; version-level sample and estimate differ, not a separate independent study.

records.title: Agentic Much? Adoption of Coding Agents on GitHub
records.reason: 2026-04-08 v2 precursor to accepted ACM journal version; preserve numerical drift and one-study identity.

records.title: Agentic Very Much! Adoption of Coding Agent in New GitHub Projects

study_extract.design: Authors' preprint comparison of coding-agent traces in a cohort of new GitHub projects.
study_extract.population: Projects created after a previous coding-agent adoption study; abstract does not fully specify observed eligible denominator.
study_extract.outcome: Preprint reports a larger estimated agent-use signal in its new-project frame; it is not a causal quality/productivity study.
study_extract.limitations: Preprint, differing time/sample frame, trace-based sensitivity and reuse of authors' earlier methodology; no independent replication.

records.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity

study_extract.design: METR-reported randomized within-developer AI-allowed/disallowed task comparison.
study_extract.population: 16 experienced OSS developers completed 246 mature-project tasks in February–June 2025; original paper site.
study_extract.outcome: Publisher reports 19% longer task time under AI-allowed assignment in this specific experienced-maintainer sample.
study_extract.limitations: Preprint/research nonprofit report, participant/task selection and tool vintage limit transport to other settings; not a universal AI slowdown.

records.title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design

study_extract.design: Research-group methods update identifying task-submission refusal and parallel-agent time measurement biases.
study_extract.population: Later 2025 follow-up involved 10 original and 47 new developers; self-selection affects reported later effect.
study_extract.outcome: Authors explicitly warn the later AI effect estimate is unreliable due to nonparticipation and concurrent work measurement.
study_extract.limitations: Not peer-reviewed efficacy replication; do not contrast point estimates from selected populations as a clean longitudinal causal trend.

records.title: The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's more to it than you think.

study_extract.design: Conceptual ACM Queue multidimensional developer-productivity measurement framework.
study_extract.population: Practice-oriented conceptual framework rather than randomized task sample.
study_extract.outcome: Defines satisfaction, performance, activity, communication and efficiency dimensions to operationalize before measurement.
study_extract.limitations: No estimate of AI effects, security quality, lifecycle energy or externally verified OSS use.
